question.prompt: If \(1<a<3\), simplifying \(\sqrt{(a-1)^2}+\sqrt{(a-3)^2}\) gives a constant. What is this constant?

solutions.explanation: Since \(a-1>0\) and \(a-3<0\), the original expression equals \((a-1)+(3-a)=2\).
solutions.title: Use the signs of the inner expressions

solutions.explanation: Using \(\sqrt{x^2}=|x|\), the two terms are the distances from \(a\) to \(1\) and from \(a\) to \(3\) on the number line. Since \(1<a<3\), these distances are the lengths of two adjacent segments that together form the segment from \(1\) to \(3\). Their sum is therefore \(3-1=2\), so the constant is \(2\).
solutions.title: Interpret the terms as distances
